How to reduce a PDF to under 1 MB

Open Compress, choose To a size and pick 1 MB. It shrinks the photos inside as gently as it can and stops as soon as the file is under 1 MB.

Compress →Free. Nothing is uploaded.

How to do it

  1. Open Compress and add your PDF.
  2. Choose To a size.
  3. Pick 1 MB.
  4. Press Compress it.
  5. Save the new file, which is named with the size it is under.

Where a 1 MB limit comes from

Many government, university and job portals allow 1 MB or 2 MB per document. A scanned file of ten pages from a phone can easily be 10 MB or more, because each page is a full-size photo. Shrinking the photos is usually enough to reach 1 MB without the pages looking any different on screen.

If the limit is 2 MB or more

Choose Other and type the size in KB: 2000 for 2 MB, 5000 for 5 MB. We count 1 MB as 1,000 KB, so a file made under 2000 KB is under 2 MB however the portal counts.

When one file will never fit

A long scanned book may not fit in 1 MB and stay readable. If the portal takes several uploads, Split by size cuts it into parts that each fit. If it only needs some pages, Extract pages keeps just those.

Questions people ask

How long does it take?

Seconds for a few pages; longer for a big scan on an older phone, because your own device does the work. A progress line shows what it is doing.

Can I compress a password-protected PDF?

Yes. Type its password when asked. The smaller file keeps the same password.

Is it really free?

Yes. No payment, no sign-up and no limit on how many files you compress.

Your file stays on your device. Foolscap does the work inside your browser, so nothing is uploaded and there is nothing for anyone to keep. How you can check
